correctness.rationale: The domain is the real symmetric Loewner band, with maximum absolute entry on both inputs and outputs. Independently, center each resolvent at m=(r_a+r_b)/2: R=mI+((r_a−r_b)/2)M with M a symmetric spectral contraction. Each row of M has Euclidean norm at most one, hence absolute row sum at most √n. This gives exactly q=r_b+c_n(r_a−r_b). The resolvent identity bounds the two-input difference by the integral of q² times ||A−B||_max. The displayed P is the positive rank-one projector onto the normalized sum of e_1 and the uniform unit vector; the resolvent at aP+b(I−P) is entrywise nonnegative with the required first row sum. The all-ones direction attains its derivative integral in the (1,1) entry. Moving inside the band by ε and taking a perturbation h<ε/n gives admissible distinct pairs and recovers the boundary derivative in the double limit, also for n=1. Integration of q² gives the three claimed terms. At fixed r>1 the leading coefficient is positive by a nonzero square integral; at b/a=1+x/√n the scaled integrand is dominated by a multiple of (1+t)^−2 and tends to [1/(1+t)+x/(2(1+t)^2)]², giving the claimed polynomial integral. These are bounded-critical and fixed-band regimes, not an exhaustive two-rate dichotomy for intervening widths. RESULT.md lines 28–84 prove the claims; checker.py and VERIFICATION.md were read but the 625 reported numerical comparisons were not rerun.

evidence: The absolutely-monotone theorem states a sharp all-n coefficient on 0≼X≼dI for every nonnegative-coefficient power series of radius >d, using the same norm on real symmetric inputs and outputs. The transformed log belongs to that class.

The related Laplace-transform theorem gives an exact constant on a negative half-line cone; it does not give a finite two-ended band constant. Standard Loewner integral representation also does not by itself state a sharp max-entry theorem.

For the transformed log, g′(d)=b/a, g′(0)=1 and [g(d)−g(0)]/d=log(b/a)/d, so dividing by b gives the frozen formula identically.

The fixed-r limit keeps the degree-two part in c. For ε=x/√n, insert (1+ε)^−1=1−ε+ε²+O(ε³) and log(1+ε)/ε=1−ε/2+ε²/3+O(ε³) in the exact formula. The cubic-and-higher remainder is O(nε³)=o(1) and the result is 1+x/2+x²/12. No separate stability optimization is needed for either limit.
